preamble: Fronting of the postalveolar/palatal affricate /tʃ/ to the dental-alveolar affricate /ts/ keeps the affricate manner and voicing and only moves the place of articulation forward. It occurs independently in several South Asian lineages: Kashmiri and other Dardic languages, Nepali (where the inherited palatal series is pronounced [ts tsʰ dz dzʱ]) and Telugu (where native /tʃ/ became [ts] before non-front vowels, producing a later phonemic split once loanwords reintroduced [tʃ]). In Europe the same change is the Chakavian 'cakavism' of Istria and several Adriatic islands, where č is replaced by c. Polish mazurzenie is filed under the retroflex cell ʈʂ → ts (cz/sz/ż/dż [t͡ʂ ʂ ʐ d͡ʐ] > c/s/z/dz), not here.

examples.note: Turner's ċ marks the Kashmiri dental affricate /ts/ that regularly continues Old Indo-Aryan c (CDIAL 4655).
The Nepali reflexes of the Old Indo-Aryan palatal affricates are alveolar affricates: च [ts], छ [tsʰ], ज [dz], झ [dzʱ].
Spelled with the palatal letter च but pronounced with [ts].

Native /tʃ/ and /dʒ/ became [ts] and [dz] before non-front vowels while staying [tʃ dʒ] before i and e (cf. చిన్న cinna [tʃinna] 'small'); loanwords with [tʃ] before back vowels later made the contrast phonemic.
In the non-palatal Chakavian of eastern Istria (Labin area), Bakar, Trogir and islands such as Vis, Hvar town and Baška on Krk, č [tʃ] is replaced by c [ts].
